mainEntity.name: What does a crypto PR agency in Vietnam actually do?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Vietnam-focused crypto PR service places your project in Vietnamese-language media and community channels, builds relationships with local KOLs and community admins, and coordinates that local presence with your global tier-1 coverage. Vietnam ranks in the top three countries globally for crypto adoption, so the market matters for user acquisition, exchange listings and community growth, not just brand awareness. Shilika Jain covers Vietnam as part of a six-market APAC practice.

mainEntity.name: How much does Vietnam crypto PR cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fractional senior operator covering Vietnam as part of an APAC retainer runs $5K–$12K/month, versus $15K–$45K/month at a traditional multi-person agency. A focused Vietnam launch sprint, covering media outreach and community activation around a single moment such as a listing or TGE, runs $15K–$40K over four to eight weeks. KOL activations are budgeted separately: nano-influencers in the Vietnamese community range from $200–$1.5K per post, micro from $500–$5K and mid-tier from $10K–$30K.

mainEntity.name: Which Vietnamese outlets and channels can you reach?

acceptedAnswer.text: On the media side: CoinCu News, BeInCrypto Vietnam, CryptoViet, and the Vietnamese editions of major regional outlets. Community channels carry as much weight: the leading Vietnamese crypto Telegram groups (some with 50K-plus active members) and the Facebook communities where retail traders in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi actually discover projects. Coverage depends on a real news hook, not a wire blast.

mainEntity.name: What is the process and how long does it take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first two weeks cover a market read, narrative localisation and KOL mapping specific to Vietnam. Week three is coordinated outreach: global embargo timed to Vietnam community drops. The first coverage typically lands within three to four weeks of starting. For ongoing retainers, the Vietnam presence compounds over two to three months as community relationships deepen and editorial contacts become familiar with the project.
